references.text: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. This is a recurring theme throughout the plagues.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened after another plague, showing the same pattern of resistance against God.
Pharaoh hardened his own heart and would not listen to Moses and Aaron, the same pattern as in 9:7.
Pharaoh also hardened his heart this time and would not let the people go, using identical wording.
Pharaoh sinned again and hardened his heart, he and his officials, and did not release the Israelites.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the Israelites leave. A continuation of the theme of hardening of the heart.
God predicted that He would harden Pharaoh's heart so that he would not let the people go.
The Lord made a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, which Pharaoh verified by sending messengers.
The Lord makes a difference between Egypt and Israel, the same theme of God's protection of His people.
Paul cites Pharaoh's hardening as an example of God's sovereignty and human resistance.
Direct narrative continuation of the same event with identical theological focus on God's rule over Pharaoh's will.
A thematic parallel illustrating Pharaoh's persistent resistance and the dynamic between his own stubbornness and God's plan.
A summarizing reference confirming that Pharaoh's resistance was part of God's plan to display signs and wonders.
A consequence reference showing how Pharaoh's inflexibility led to his own downfall at the Red Sea.
Strengthens understanding of the recurring pattern where God's action hardens Pharaoh's heart.
